facts.fact: According to eMarketer, programmatic ad spending will account for 86.5% of all digital ad dollars in 2021.
facts.quote: programmatic ad spending will account for 86.5% of all digital ad dollars in 2021

facts.fact: In a second-price auction, the highest bidder wins but pays only $0.01 above the second-highest bid.
facts.quote: the highest bidder wins, however, only pays $0.01 above the second highest bid

facts.fact: The majority of publishers in the programmatic ecosystem use four selling strategies: open exchange, private auction, preferred deal, and programmatic guaranteed.
facts.quote: The majority of the publishers in the programmatic ecosystem use four selling strategies

facts.fact: In programmatic guaranteed (PG), the advertiser pays a flat negotiated CPM for the inventory it purchases, per StackAdapt's description.
facts.quote: The advertiser pays a flat negotiated CPM for the inventory that they are purchasing.

facts.fact: StackAdapt says a programmatic guaranteed deal is best used when the advertiser has a set allocated budget it can commit to buying all relevant impressions, negotiated at a flat CPM within a set date range.
facts.quote: negotiated at a flat CPM with a publisher within a set date range

facts.fact: In programmatic guaranteed, the publisher sets aside or reserves inventory for the advertiser in return for the advertiser purchasing all impressions that fit the set criteria.
facts.quote: In return for purchasing all of the impressions fulfilling the criteria set, the publisher will set aside or reserve inventory for the advertiser.

facts.fact: StackAdapt states there are four fundamental types of programmatic ad inventory.
facts.quote: Having a solid understanding of the four fundamental types of programmatic ad inventory
